newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity settles lower in narrow trading.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity settles lower in narrow trading.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled lower Tuesday in narrow trading as the complex was pressured by moderate temperatures in the western U.S., declining cash prices and an ongoing skid in natural gas futures.
"It's been a pretty dull day. It was off this morning. Then, there was a little bit of a bounce," said an East Coast broker.

February California-Oregon Border (COB) futures finished down 24 cents at $13.15 a megawatt hour (MWh) after finding support at $13.00, its life-of-contract low for a second day. The contract fell $2.28 or 14.8 percent from a week ago.
March COB ended off only one cent at $11.49. Most deferred months were untraded.
February Palo Verde (PV) futures settled down 45 cents at $15.34/MWh after touching a low of $15.05. It was $2.14 or 12.2 percent lower than a week ago.
March PV ended down 10 cents at $13.60. Other active outer-month PV contracts finished lower.
The electricity complex downtrend is also underpinned by above-normal precipitation, both rain and snow, in major hydroelectric reserve areas in the Pacific Northwest.
In the Northwest, coastal rains and mountain snows are predicted to continue through Wednesday. Temperatures in the region would moderate to slightly above normal levels by the end of the week.

In the Southwest, temperatures are expected to average near normal for the rest of the week with scattered showers in New Mexico, northern California and southern Arizona over the next couple of days.
The natural gas market continued to suffer sharp losses across the board on mild temperature outlook for next week.
NYMEX February Henry Hub natural gas futures finished down 15.4 cents at $2.916 per million British thermal units after hitting an intraday low of $2.830.

February gas deliveries to the San Juan/Blanco Hub were assessed near $2.55/mmBtu, down from Monday's $2.70-$2.75. Swing gas prices at the Southwest delivery point finished the day at $2.75, down about 15 cents from Monday.
At the U.S.-Canadian border, swing gas prices at the Sumas trading point stepped down five to 10 cents to $2.30-$2.39.
A 500 kilvolt transmission line, which runs from Snohomish County, Wash. to the Canadian border, could stay down until next week after damage from an ice storm late last week.

The outage of the 350 megawatt (MW) unit 1 at the Comanche coal-fired power plant in Pueblo, Colorado, was extended to approximately January 29 as more time was needed to repair damages from a fire in mid-December.
